findings.F1: In rising markets the edge of a close above the prior 20-day high grows with the horizon, while closes below the high give nothing. Above-high cases return, in excess of drift: +3.08 % over 3 days (151 cases, 63 days, pooled t 1.14), +6.36 % over 5 days (74 cases, 32 days, pooled t 2.54, strength 0.98) and +12.25 % over 10 days (38 cases, 15 days, pooled t 2.21, strength 1.11). Below-high cases return +0.41 %, −0.55 % and −1.39 % over the same horizons, with every t under 1 in absolute value. Removing DOGE leaves the effect intact: +6.82 % at 5 days, t 2.87.
findings.F2: Within the above-high cases, the distance above the high does not rank the outcome. The Spearman correlation of distance with the scaled excess return is 0.03 at 3 days (p 0.73), −0.04 at 5 days (p 0.72) and 0.31 at 10 days (p 0.056). Entry-forecast quartiles of the book's trades are not monotone either: 6.8 %, 7.1 %, 22.4 % and 12.3 % per trade.
findings.F3: Outside rising markets, the further a close sits below its 20-day high in swings, the lower the next 3 days. The Spearman correlation is 0.112 (p 0.0002, 1103 cases). Pooled-by-day excess returns by distance in swings are:
findings.F4: This downward drift far below the high is strongest in choppy markets. Choppy cases 4 to 8 swings below the high return −3.68 % over 3 days (69 cases, t −3.16 unpooled), and those 2 to 4 swings below return −1.29 % (104 cases, t −2.10). Choppy cases at least 4 swings below give −3.49 % pooled (41 days, t −1.94); the same cases in falling markets give −1.44 % (99 days, t −1.42). The deep cases outside rising markets are negative in 9 of the 12 windows, including all six windows with 44 or more cases (w7, w9, w12–w15).
findings.F5: In rising markets, coins far below their high do not fall. Cases 4 to 8 swings below return −0.74 % over 3 days (t −0.59), and cases 2 to 4 below return +0.58 % (t 0.78). The weakness far below the high therefore belongs to non-rising markets, not to the brief's rising one.
findings.F6: The book's gain is concentrated in a few days. The top 1 % of its 1449 days carry 88 % of the total summed daily gain, and the top 5 % carry 181 %. The mean daily return ranges from −0.017 % to +0.243 % across windows w7–w18, and 4 of the 12 windows are negative.

ideas.idea: In a rising market, the nearer a coin's daily close comes to its 20-day high, and the further it stands above it, measured in units of its daily swing over the last 20 days, the more it rises over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: In a rising market, a trader holds breakouts above the recent high for one to two weeks rather than three days, and expects nothing from coins left below their high.
ideas.name: rising breakout ten-day drift

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the further a coin's daily close sits below its 20-day high, measured in units of its daily swing over the last 20 days, the more it falls over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: In a choppy market, a trader avoids buying, or sells, coins that have slipped many swings below their recent high, and leans harder the deeper the slip.
ideas.name: choppy far-below-high decline

ideas.idea: In a falling market, the further a coin's daily close sits below its 20-day high, measured in units of its daily swing over the last 20 days, the more it falls over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: In a falling market, a trader refuses to bottom-fish coins that are several swings under their recent high and treats the depth of the slip as a reason to stay short.
ideas.name: falling far-below-high decline
